args.title: checkout-api: health check failures on v2.3.1, rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
The latest deploy of checkout-api (v2.3.1) was failing health checks in production with an elevated error rate of ~18% across all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west). The service was rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production (the intervening v2.3.1-rc entry was staging-only and also unhealthy).

Rollout detail: the first rollback attempt halted after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving the service in a mixed state (us-east on v2.3.0, us-west and eu-west still on v2.3.1). A retry of the rollback completed successfully across all regions.

Current state: all three production regions are on v2.3.0, service is healthy, and error rate has dropped to ~0.2%. v2.3.1 should not be redeployed until the cause of the health check failures is identified and fixed.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
The incident did go through despite the timeout — no duplicate needed. Task complete.

## Summary

**Diagnosis:** checkout-api was on v2.3.1 in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), unhealthy with an ~18% error rate.

**Target version selection:** Deployment history showed v2.3.0 as the most recent release healthy in production. Note the list contained a `v2.3.1-rc` entry with a *higher* sequence number (seq 2) than v2.3.1's seq 3 — that was a staging deployment, not production, so it was correctly excluded as a rollback target.

**Rollback:**
- First attempt failed with `partial_failure` — halted after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving a mixed state (us-east on v2.3.0; us-west and eu-west still on the bad v2.3.1).
- Retried the rollback; it completed successfully across all regions.

**Verification:** All three regions now on v2.3.0, service healthy, error rate down to ~0.2%.

**Incident:** Opened **INC-0001** (SEV2) documenting the failure, both rollback attempts including the partial-failure/mixed state, the final healthy state, and a note that v2.3.1 should not be redeployed until the root cause is understood.

Two things worth flagging:
- The rollback required a retry to converge — the orchestrator error on the first pass is worth investigating, since a halt between regions leaves the fleet on split versions.
- The create_incident call returned a 30s timeout but had actually succeeded. I checked with `list_incidents` rather than blindly retrying; the idempotency key would have prevented a duplicate, but confirming avoided a second page to on-call.
